question.text: What stage will the BCP have reached in disposing of Ueno Bank's assets and liabilities before November 28, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria:
Resolution is based on public announcements made by the Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP) or its intervention team for Ueno Bank S.A. on or before 27 November 2026 (Paraguay time, UTC-3), as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Announcements first made on 28 November 2026 or later do not count.

- "Tender launched": the BCP has publicly issued a call for bids, published the terms (bases/pliego) of a licitación, or otherwise made public that a bidding process is open for financial institutions to bid for portfolios (lotes) of Ueno Bank S.A.'s assets and/or liabilities, including deposits. A restricted or invitation-only process counts once it has been publicly announced, even if invitations were sent to selected banks earlier.
- "Recipient institution named": the BCP has publicly designated at least one specific named institution (a bank, finance company, newly created bridge bank, or public entity) that is to receive or assume a portion of Ueno Bank S.A.'s assets, liabilities, deposits or client portfolio as part of the resolution, whether through a BCP board resolution, an adjudication/award announcement, an official communiqué, or a statement by the BCP president or the intervention team at a public press conference reported by credible sources.

Select "No tender launched and no recipient institution named" if neither had occurred by that date; "A tender has been launched, but no recipient institution named" if a tender had been launched and no institution named; and "At least one recipient institution has been named" if at least one institution had been named, whether or not a tender was launched. A compilation of the BCP's official communiqués on the case is maintained by ABC Color at https://www.abc.com.py/economia/2026/11/04/todos-los-comunicados-del-bcp-sobre-ueno-bank/ and the BCP's own newsroom is at bcp.gov.py.
question.fine_print: Banks named only as payment agents or channels for Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos payouts, or merely listed as places where former Ueno Bank clients may collect funds or open new accounts, are not recipient institutions. Announcements concerning Ueno Casa de Bolsa (a separate brokerage) or Ueno's fund-management company do not count, even if their client portfolios are transferred to other firms. Statements of intent or of ongoing negotiations, and completion of the balance de exclusión, do not on their own constitute a tender launch or the naming of a recipient institution.

research:
I've finished searching and am now writing the summary.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The ABC Color compilation was last updated 05 Nov. The last entry is the 5 Nov communiqué on FGD payouts to the "primer grupo" of depositors. It has nothing on a tender, bid terms (bases) or a recipient bank. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/economia/2026/11/04/todos-los-comunicados-del-bcp-sobre-ueno-bank/)
- I could not find any BCP communiqué calling bids or naming a recipient institution for Ueno Bank lots. I did not read bcp.gov.py directly.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. As of 15-16 Nov, no tender has been launched and no recipient has been named.
- 2026-11-15: FGD director José Maciel said the BCP is "studying" moving assets and liabilities in lots to interested banks, "todavía sin fechas ni entidades confirmadas." The Hoy article calls this a direct cession to interested banks and does not mention a formal licitación. Under the fine print, that is still only a statement of intent. [Hoy](https://www.hoy.com.py/nacionales/2026/11/15/bcp-busca-que-otros-bancos-absorban-depositos-de-ueno-mediante-cesion)
- 2026-11-15: Infobae/EFE says lots "will be offered" to other institutions. It names no banks and gives no dates. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/15/lo-que-se-sabe-y-lo-que-viene-despues-de-la-intervencion-de-ueno-bank-en-paraguay/)
- 2026-11-14: About 32,000 retirees were reassigned to eight banks, which began issuing new debit cards. These banks act as payment channels, so the fine print likely excludes them as recipient institutions. [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/paraguay-banks-replace-cards-ueno-pensioners-601341)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Coverage centres on pensioners and mutual-fund investors who are still waiting. There is nothing on a tender. [BioBioChile](https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/internacional/america-latina/2026/11/16/miles-de-jubilados-siguen-afectados-por-la-crisis-de-ueno-bank-en-paraguay.shtml)
- 2026-11-14: The first FGD stage was completed: 1,812,348 savers received about G. 3.99 trillion (about USD 643m). Reporting mentions a legal deadline of 17 Nov. [AsiaToday](https://asiatoday.id/read/all-ueno-depositors-repaid-in-part-as-paraguay-nears-17-november-deadline)
- 2026-11-13: A court froze the assets of three former BCP executives. This adds political and legal pressure on the bank. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/policiales/2026/11/14/ueno-bank-ordenan-inhibir-bienes-y-embargar-cuentas-de-exdirectivos-del-bcp/)
- 2026-11-12: Schreiner reported about USD 600m in sound assets and said the exclusion balance would take another 8-10 days, followed by a licitación of lots to several banks. One outlet says the tender would happen "a más tardar, a fin de mes." [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.py/negocios/2026/11/12/bcp-anuncia-que-distribuira-por-lotes-en-bancos-locales-los-activos-y-pasivos-de-ueno-bank/), [ADN](https://www.adndigital.com.py/bcp-distribuira-activos-y-depositos-de-ueno-entre-varios-bancos-para-avanzar-con-la-resolucion/), [Hoy](https://www.hoy.com.py/nacionales/2026/11/12/bcp-confirma-hallazgo-de-usd-600-millones-en-activos-sanos-de-ueno-bank-y-priorizara-fondos-previsionales)

## 4. Base rates
- Cefisa, the most recent comparable case under Ley 2334: the BCP board started resolution on 2022-12-06. On 2023-01-06 (Res. N° 14), it named Bancop, Banco Río, Banco Basa, Finexpar and Tu Financiera as recipients after a "competitive and transparent process." That is about 31 days from start to naming recipients. The article does not give the tender's launch date. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/economia/2023/01/09/transferiran-activos-y-pasivos-de-cefisa-a-3-bancos-y-dos-financieras/)
- Applying that 31-day gap to Ueno (start 2026-11-02) points to about 3 Dec, after the 27 Nov cutoff. Ueno is far larger and more complex, but there is also more political urgency.
- Ára (financiera, around 2022-23): the BCP asked for bids with a short window ("hasta este viernes 5") and then partly adjudicated the assets. That suggests offer windows can run about one week. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/edicion-impresa/economia/adjudican-parte-de-activos-de-ara-1373175.html)
- In both earlier cases, the public record often shows the recipients when the award is announced, without a separately publicised tender launch.
- The law's 15-day deadline for the exclusion balance points to about 17 Nov.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied relate to this question: they cover the Fed, BoE, Woori and others. I found no prediction market or expert forecast on the Ueno tender or recipients.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 17 Nov: the statutory 15-day deadline for the exclusion balance, and the reported legal deadline tied to FGD payouts.
- About 20-22 Nov: Schreiner's estimate for finishing the exclusion balance.
- About 27 Nov / "fin de mes": the reported target for the tender or the transfer of lots.
- 30 Nov: the suspension of late-interest charges on Ueno loans ends. That could prompt an announcement on who will service the loan portfolio.
- Things to watch:
  - a BCP communiqué publishing bid terms (bases) or inviting bids;
  - any decision to place the pension-fund (IPS) portion directly with named banks;
  - a board resolution naming recipients, as happened with Cefisa.

As of 16 November no tender has been launched and no institution has been named to take over any part of Ueno Bank. Officials keep saying they plan to sell the bank's portfolios in lots (lotes) to several local banks through a tender (licitación). On 15 November the director of the deposit guarantee fund (FGD) still described the transfer plan as under study, "with no dates or entities confirmed yet."

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16 (when I checked): the ABC Color compilation of BCP communiqués (dated 2026-11-05, still being updated) covers the start of the resolution, the FGD advance payments, released payment aliases, mutual fund suspensions, staff severance and the payout platforms. I searched it for "licita", "lote", "exclusi", "transfer", "adjudic" and "cesi" and found nothing about a tender, an exclusion balance or a transfer. ## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles or nearly settles the question.
- 2026-11-14: about 32,000 IPS pensioners who were paid through Ueno were moved to eight other banks, which started handing out replacement debit cards. IPS calls this a one-time emergency measure, and the banks were not named in the report. This looks like a payment-channel role, which the fine print excludes, not a takeover of Ueno's liabilities. [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/paraguay-banks-replace-cards-ueno-pensioners-601341)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

The transfer depends on cleaning up the bank and finishing the accounting verification, and is "todavía sin fechas ni entidades confirmadas" (still without dates or confirmed entities). The winners would take over the loan collection rights and the pending deposits. Savers in the second stage (up to 75 minimum wages) must wait for the exclusion balance. No dates or banks were given. [Infobae/EFE](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/15/lo-que-se-sabe-y-lo-que-viene-despues-de-la-intervencion-de-ueno-bank-en-paraguay/)
- 2026-11-14: the BCP said all 1,812,348 covered savers had received the advance, about G. 3.99 trillion (around USD 643 million). One outlet mentions a 17 November legal deadline. [Asia Today](https://asiatoday.id/read/all-ueno-depositors-repaid-in-part-as-paraguay-nears-17-november-deadline)
- 2026-11-13: a court froze assets of three former BCP executives. This is a separate investigation. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/policiales/2026/11/14/ueno-bank-ordenan-inhibir-bienes-y-embargar-cuentas-de-exdirectivos-del-bcp/)
- 2026-11-12: BCP president Jorge Schreiner reported about USD 600 million in "sound assets." He said the BCP will "probably tender in lots" spread across as many banks as possible, with no "megabanco," and expected a "much clearer picture" in about 10 days. The FGD can cover any gap between assets and liabilities. Reports target the transfers for late November, depending on the final asset valuation and how much the interested banks can absorb. [ABC/EFE](https://www.abc.com.py/internacionales/2026/11/12/banco-central-estima-en-600-millones-de-dolares-los-activos-sanos-en-ueno-bank/); [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.py/negocios/2026/11/12/bcp-anuncia-que-distribuira-por-lotes-en-bancos-locales-los-activos-y-pasivos-de-ueno-bank/); [Última Hora](https://www.ultimahora.com/bcp-dice-que-los-fondos-jubilatorios-se-pueden-cubrir-con-activos-sanos-de-ueno-bank); [economia.com.py](https://economia.com.py/el-bcp-preve-cubrir-con-activos-sanos-los-fondos-previsionales-atrapados-en-ueno-bank-y-licitara-la-cartera-entre-varios-bancos/)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no usable precedent for how long past Ley 2334/03 resolutions in Paraguay took to get from exclusion balance to tender to award. My one search on this returned only unrelated Peruvian results.
- By law the exclusion balance closes 15 days after the process starts, so around 17 November. Officials' own estimates put the exclusion balance at about 20-22 November and the tender and transfer at about 27 November or "late November."
- Official timelines have already slipped. On 12 November the tender looked about 10-15 days away. By 15 November officials were giving no dates at all.
- Under the resolution rules, a tender would normally be publicly launched before anyone is named. A direct placement of the pension-fund portion with named banks could skip that step, but no source says this is planned.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction markets supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) relate to Ueno Bank or Paraguay. They are all unrelated.
- I found no Metaculus community forecast or expert forecast on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 November
- Around 17 November: the 15-day statutory deadline for the exclusion balance.
- About 20-22 November: Schreiner's estimate for a clearer picture of the exclusion balance.
- Around 27 November: the reported target for the tender and portfolio transfer. This is the last day that counts; anything first announced on 28 November is too late.
- 30 November: late-interest and penalty charges on Ueno loans and cards stay suspended until this date, after the resolution window.
- Also in play: the CDA holder validation (registrocda.bcp.gov.py), pressure from pensioners and IPS for quick action, and Fitch's negative watch on Paraguay. These could speed things up.
- Watch out for: Ueno Casa de Bolsa or Ueno AFPISA portfolio transfers, and banks named only as FGD payment agents or pension card issuers. None of these count under the fine print.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 11.5 days remain, through 27 November 2026 (Paraguay time). The question resolves around 28 November.

(b) **Status quo:** As of 15-16 November, no tender had been called and no recipient institution had been named. On 15 November the FGD director said the BCP is "studying" a transfer in lots, "todavía sin fechas ni entidades confirmadas" (still with no dates or institutions confirmed). If nothing changes, the answer is option A.

(c) **Base rates:**
- In the Cefisa resolution, the BCP named recipients 31 days after the resolution started. The same gap for Ueno points to about 3 December, after the cutoff.
- In both Cefisa and Ára, bid windows were short, around one week. Recipients mostly became public at the award stage, without a separately publicised tender launch. So the "tender launched but no one named" state is often never publicly visible.
- Ueno is far larger and more complex than either case, which argues for slower progress. Political urgency is much higher, with the sovereign rating on negative watch and pension funds exposed, which argues for faster progress.
- Official timelines in such crises usually slip.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 12 November: Schreiner said the exclusion balance needed another 8-10 days, followed by a licitación of lots to several banks. One outlet said the tender would happen "a más tardar, a fin de mes" (at the latest by the end of the month), and another put the transfer about 15 days out, around 27 November.
- 15 November: Maciel said there were no dates or entities yet and described a direct cession to interested banks rather than a formal tender.
- 15-16 November: the ABC compilation and other coverage show nothing on bid terms or awards.
- "End of month" sits right at or just after the 27 November cutoff, so even the stated plan barely fits the window.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenario:** Under pressure over the IPS money and the 30 November end of the late-charge suspension, the BCP board could quickly assign the pension-fund deposits and sound assets directly to named banks. Those could include public Banco Nacional de Fomento or a bridge vehicle, which would resolve the question as option C before any formal tender. Alternatively, Schreiner could announce at a press conference that banks have been invited to bid, which would make it option B.

**Moves from the base rate:** I start from roughly 60% status quo, based on the Cefisa timing and Ueno's complexity. I moved down to about 45% because of the explicit end-of-month target and the high urgency. The remaining probability is split roughly evenly between a publicised tender and a direct naming of recipients, since direct cession may skip a formal tender.

Option_A: 0.45
Option_B: 0.28
Option_C: 0.27

(a) **Time left:** About 11 days. Announcements count only if made on or before 27 November 2026 (Paraguay time), and the question resolves around 28 November.

(b) **Status quo:** As of 15-16 November no tender had been launched and no recipient institution had been named. On 15 November the FGD director said there were still "no dates or entities confirmed." If nothing changes, the answer is "No tender launched and no recipient institution named."

(c) **Base rates:**
- **Cefisa** is the closest precedent under Ley 2334. Resolution started 6 December 2022, and recipients (Bancop, Río, Basa, Finexpar, Tu Financiera) were named by board resolution on 6 January 2023. That is about 31 days, with no separately publicised tender launch beforehand.
- The same gap applied to Ueno (start 2 November) points to about 3 December, after the cutoff.
- **Ára** shows offer windows can be short, about one week.
- In both earlier cases the public record shows recipients at the award stage rather than at a separately announced tender launch. That structurally lowers the odds of option B.
- Ueno is vastly larger and more complex than either case, which argues for slower progress. But political urgency is far higher: IPS money, pensioners, the Fitch watch and court action against former BCP officials.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **12 November:** Schreiner said the exclusion balance would take 8-10 more days (about 20-22 November), followed by a tender of lots to several banks. One outlet said the tender would come "a más tardar, a fin de mes."
- **12 November:** Diario HOY reported the tender and transfer about 15 days out, around 27 November, right at the cutoff.
- **15 November:** The FGD director described the BCP as "studying" a direct cession of lots to interested banks, without dates or entities. This suggests no imminent public tender call. If they go the cession route, a direct naming could skip the tender stage entirely.
- **14 November:** The banks that took on retirees are payment channels and do not count as recipients.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:**
- The BCP fast-tracks the pension-fund (IPS) portion by board resolution, naming two or three large domestic banks to assume those deposits and matching sound assets around 25-27 November, before the formal tender for the remaining lots. That resolves "recipient named."
- Alternatively, the BCP publishes tender terms around 24-26 November with offers due in early December, which resolves option B.

**Reasoning:** I start from the Cefisa timing, which falls just past the cutoff, and from the status quo. Officials' own targets sit right at the deadline, and such targets usually slip. Ueno's size is another reason for delay. The strong political pressure, and the chance of direct naming of banks for the pension portion, push the other way. Because past practice tends to reveal recipients at award rather than announcing a tender separately, B gets less weight than its intermediate position might suggest. I moved modestly away from "status quo near-certain" toward C because of explicit end-of-month targets and the high urgency.

Option_A: 0.47
Option_B: 0.19
Option_C: 0.34

(a) **Time left:** About 11.5 days. Only BCP announcements made on or before 27 November 2026 (Paraguay time) count.

(b) **Status quo:** As of 15-16 November, no tender had been called and no recipient institution had been named. On 15 November, FGD director Maciel said the BCP is still "studying" a cession in lots, "todavía sin fechas ni entidades confirmadas." If nothing changes, the first option resolves.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Cefisa, the closest precedent under Ley 2334: resolution started 6 December 2022, and recipients were named on 6 January 2023. That is 31 days, and no separately publicised tender came first.
- Applying the same gap to Ueno (start 2 November) gives about 3 December, which is after the cutoff.
- Ára: the BCP used roughly one-week bid windows, again mostly visible only at adjudication.
- Officials' timelines in large bank resolutions usually slip, and Ueno is vastly larger and more complex than Cefisa. Both points argue for delay.
- In these precedents, tenders are often not publicised before the award. That makes "tender launched but nobody named" a narrower window than it first appears.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 12 November: Schreiner said the exclusion balance needs 8-10 more days, followed by a licitación by lots. One outlet said the tender would come "a más tardar, a fin de mes." Other reporting put the transfer around 27 November.
- 15 November: officials were still giving no dates and naming no entities, and talked of direct cession rather than a formal tender.
- Several things create pressure to act quickly:
  - the statutory 15-day exclusion-balance deadline (about 17 November);
  - Fitch's negative watch on the sovereign rating (11 November);
  - the pension-fund priority;
  - the 30 November end of the late-interest suspension.
- Together these make a pre-cutoff announcement plausible, perhaps an early direct placement of the IPS or pension portion with named banks.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** Facing political pressure, the BCP board quickly adopts a resolution before 27 November. It places the IPS or pension deposits and matched sound assets with two or three named banks by direct cession, with no published tender. That would resolve as "recipient named." Alternatively, the BCP publicly invites banks to bid around 24-26 November, with the award due in early December, which would resolve as "tender launched."

**Adjustment:** I start from the status quo and the Cefisa timing, which together suggest about 60% for no action by the cutoff. I move down to about 47% because officials explicitly targeted the end of the month and political urgency is unusually high.
